title: From Classical to Deep Learning: A Hybrid CNN-Ensemble Framework for Intrusion Detection in Internet of Medical Things
authors: Faris Kateb;Owais Khan;Fazal Qudus Khan
country: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan  (lead affiliation: King Abdulaziz University)
domain_cat: Intrusion / anomaly detection in Medical IoT and healthcare networks — IoMT healthcare cybersecurity intrusion detection
objectives: Build a multi-dataset benchmark comparing classical ML and deep learning for IoMT intrusion detection, test whether a hybrid CNN-ensemble improves detection, and measure cross-dataset transfer.
contribution: Two-stage hybrid CNN-Ensemble classifying both raw features and a 64-dimensional CNN-extracted representation with Random Forest and XGBoost, averaging their probabilities; two-stage SHAP + RFE feature selection; SHAP analysis showing seven of the top 15 features are patient vital signs.
dataset: WUSTL-EHMS-2020: 16,318 records (14,272 normal; 2,046 attack = 1,124 spoofing + 922 data alteration), 35 features after cleaning, stratified 60/20/20 split, 9,790 training samples, SMOTE to 8,563 per class. Edge-IIoTset: 157,800 samples, 52 features, 14 attack types, training partition 94,680 (84.6% attack), majority downsampled to 14,581 per class. UNSW-NB15: 2,540,000 flows, 43 features, nine attack categories, training partition 1,524,028, inverse-frequency class weights (normal 0.572, attack 3.953), DL baselines on a 200,000-sample stratified subset.
models: Proposed 1D-CNN extractor (two Conv1D blocks, 32 and 64 filters) feeding RF and XGBoost on raw and CNN features (four classifiers). Baselines: Random Forest, XGBoost, DNN (128-64-32), 1D-CNN (64,128), LSTM (64,32), CNN-LSTM, CNN-BiLSTM-MHA. Ablations: raw-only and CNN-only ensembles.
training: Centralised offline supervised training on GPU (Google Colab). Batch size 256, up to 100 epochs, EarlyStopping patience 10-15, ReduceLROnPlateau factor 0.5 patience 5, binary cross-entropy with class weights, Adam. RF 100 estimators max depth 15; XGBoost 100 estimators max depth 6 lr 0.1. Decision threshold searched 0.15-0.85 on validation F1. Seed 42.
architecture: Model pipeline: raw features to two classifiers; CNN-transformed features to two more; probabilities averaged and thresholded. Deployment described generically as IoMT gateways and edge devices.
params: CNN extractor 25,728 parameters (0.10 MB); full ensemble 2.11 MB. Baseline parameter counts not reported.
hardware: Google Colab with NVIDIA GPU (model not stated). Python 3.10, TensorFlow 2.x, scikit-learn 1.x, XGBoost 1.x, SHAP, imbalanced-learn.
evaluation: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, MCC, ROC-AUC; trainable parameters, disk size, inference latency per sample, estimated FLOPs; McNemar's test on UNSW-NB15. Recall emphasised as the safety-critical metric.
baselines: Six baseline models plus CNN-BiLSTM-MHA, and raw-only and CNN-only ensemble ablations.
results: WUSTL-EHMS-2020 tuned XGBoost F1 0.914 +/- 0.013, MCC 0.916, ROC-AUC 0.994; proposed ensemble F1 0.898, MCC 0.886 (recall 84.8%, precision 95.3%); best DL baseline F1 0.649. UNSW-NB15 proposed ensemble F1 0.968 +/- 0.002, MCC 0.968, precision 0.985, recall 0.960; best baseline F1 0.957; McNemar vs RF p=0.153. Edge-IIoTset F1 = 1.000 for all models. Feature reduction 62.9% / 62.8% / 84.6%. Cross-dataset best transfer UNSW->WUSTL F1 0.603, MCC 0.609. Inference latency 111.6 ms.
validation: Stratified 60/20/20 train/validation/test; five runs with seeds 42, 123, 456, 789, 1024; mean +/- SD; threshold tuned on validation. No cross-validation.
robustness: Ablation (raw-only, CNN-only, full ensemble) on WUSTL and UNSW; six cross-dataset transfer scenarios; multiple seeds. Adversarial robustness and noise tests not reported.
strengths: Three datasets with MCC and ROC-AUC alongside F1; reports negative cross-dataset transfer honestly; shows hybrid gain is small on large data and single XGBoost wins on small data; source code, preprocessed data samples and requirements provided.
limitations: All datasets from simulated or testbed environments; zero-padding cross-dataset alignment is a worst-case baseline and domain adaptation untested; binary classification only; efficiency measured in an isolated setting, not real IoMT gateway hardware; adversarial robustness not assessed.
risks: Threat context covers spoofing, data alteration, DDoS, ransomware and MITM; notes safety-critical nature of IoMT and trust issues of opaque models. Adversarial evasion, data poisoning and privacy risks of using patient vital signs not addressed.
